title: Grade 6 Percents and Discounts
seo_title: Grade 6 Percents and Discounts Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets on percents and discounts for the BC curriculum: percent as out of 100 on hundred grids, changing between percents, fractions and decimals, percent of a number, and discounts and sale prices. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Percent means out of 100: 35% = 35/100 = 0.35. For a sale price, find the discount first, then subtract it.
key_sub: 25% off $40 is not $15: 25% of $40 is $40 ÷ 4 = $10, so the sale price is $40 − $10 = $30.
body_html:
Percent means out of 100

A percent is a number out of 100. The sign % means “out of 100”. On a hundred grid, each square is 1%, and the whole grid is 100%.

Out of another whole

Write 17 out of 50 as a percent.

Make the whole 100: 50 × 2 = 100, so 17 × 2 = 34.

Answer: 34%

Percents, fractions and decimals

A percent is a fraction with a denominator of 100. It is also a decimal in hundredths. To change a percent to a decimal, divide by 100. To change a decimal to a percent, multiply by 100.

PercentFractionDecimal
50%120.5
25%140.25
75%340.75
20%150.2
10%1100.1
5%1200.05
1%11000.01

Percent of a number

Start from easy benchmarks. 10% means divide by 10. 1% means divide by 100. 25% means divide by 4, and 50% means divide by 2. Then build the percent you need.

PercentHow to find itOf 60
10%divide by 106
5%half of 10%3
15%10% + 5%9
30%3 × 10%18
25%divide by 415
75%3 × 25%45

Discounts and sale prices

The discount is the money you save. The sale price is the price minus the discount. Find the discount first, then subtract.

Example

An $80 pair of hiking boots is 20% off. What is the sale price?

10% of $80 = $8, so 20% = $16. $80 − $16 = $64.

Answer: $64

faq.q: What do Grade 6 students learn about percents in BC?
faq.a: The BC Grade 6 math curriculum includes whole-number percents and percentage discounts. Students see a percent as a number out of 100, change between percents, fractions and decimals, find a percent of a number and work out sale prices.

faq.q: How do you find a percent of a number without a calculator?
faq.a: Use benchmarks: 10% means divide by 10, 5% is half of 10%, 25% means divide by 4 and 50% means divide by 2. Then combine them, so 15% of 60 is 6 + 3 = 9.

faq.q: How do you calculate a sale price with a percent discount?
faq.a: Find the discount first, then subtract it from the price. For 25% off $40, the discount is $10 and the sale price is $30, not $40 − $25 = $15.

faq.q: How do you change a fraction to a percent?
faq.a: Make the denominator 100. For example, 3/5 = 60/100 = 60%. If that is hard, divide the numerator by the denominator and multiply by 100: 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6, and 0.6 × 100 = 60%.

sets.title: Percent means out of 100: hundred grids

items.q: What percent of the hundred grid is shaded?
items.e: 37 of the 100 squares are shaded. 37 out of 100 = 37%. 63% is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: What percent of the hundred grid is shaded?
items.e: 6 full columns of 10 = 60 squares out of 100 = 60%. 6% counts the columns, not the squares.

items.q: What percent of the hundred grid is shaded?
items.e: Only 8 squares out of 100 are shaded: 8%. 80% would be 8 full columns.

items.q: What percent of the hundred grid is not shaded?
items.e: 45 squares are shaded, so 100 − 45 = 55 are not: 55%. 45% is the shaded part, and 145% adds 100 + 45 instead of subtracting.

items.q: What does percent mean?
items.e: Per cent means “for each hundred”. 45% means 45 out of 100.

items.q: On a hundred grid, each small square is what percent of the whole grid?
items.e: There are 100 squares, so each one is 1 out of 100 = 1%. 10% is one full column of 10.

items.q: What percent of the hundred grid is shaded?
items.e: All 100 squares are shaded. The whole is 100%.

items.q: Write 73 out of 100 as a percent.
items.e: Out of 100 is the same as percent: 73%. 27% is the other part, 100 − 73.

items.q: Which means the same as 9%?
items.e: 9% = 9 out of 100. 9 out of 10 is 90%, ten times as much.

items.q: On a hundred grid, 25% of the squares are shaded. How many squares are shaded?
items.e: 25% means 25 out of 100, so 25 squares. 75 squares are not shaded, and 4 comes from 100 ÷ 25.

items.q: How many more squares must be shaded so that 50% of the grid is shaded?
items.e: 50% is 50 squares. 12 are shaded now, so 50 − 12 = 38 more. 62 adds 50 + 12, and 50 forgets the 12 already shaded.

items.q: On a hundred grid, 30 squares are red and 45 squares are blue. The rest are white. What percent of the grid is white?
items.e: 30 + 45 = 75 squares are coloured. 100 − 75 = 25 are white: 25%. 75% is the coloured part, and 15% is 45 − 30.

items.q: The shaded squares show the cedar seedlings that grew in a school garden. What percent of the seedlings grew?
items.e: 64 of the 100 squares are shaded: 64%. 36% is the part that did not grow, and 46% swaps the digits.

items.q: A school has 100 Grade 6 students. 46 of them walk to school. What percent do not walk?
items.e: 100 − 46 = 54 students out of 100 do not walk: 54%. 46% is the walkers, and 146% adds 100 + 46 instead of subtracting.

items.q: Write 7 out of 10 as a percent.
items.e: Make the whole 100: 7 out of 10 = 70 out of 100 = 70%. 7% is only 7 out of 100.

items.q: Write 17 out of 50 as a percent.
items.e: 50 × 2 = 100, so multiply 17 by 2 too: 34 out of 100 = 34%. 17% forgets that the whole is 50, not 100.

items.q: Write 9 out of 20 as a percent.
Write 12 out of 25 as a percent.
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so 12 × 4 = 48: 48%. 12% forgets that the whole is 25. 13 is 25 − 12, and 37 is 12 + 25.

items.q: Write 3 out of 4 as a percent.
items.e: 4 × 25 = 100, so 3 × 25 = 75: 75%. 34% just writes the digits 3 and 4 together, and 25% is the 1 part left over.

items.q: Which is greater than 50%?
items.e: Change each to out of 100. 13 out of 25 = 52 out of 100 = 52%. 24 out of 50 = 48%, 4 out of 10 = 40%, and 49 out of 100 = 49%. Only 13 out of 25 is more than 50%.

items.q: Write 35% as a decimal.
items.e: 35% = 35 hundredths = 0.35. Divide by 100: move the decimal point 2 places left.

items.q: Write 7% as a decimal.
items.e: 7% = 7 hundredths = 0.07. 0.7 is 7 tenths, which is 70%.

items.q: Write 0.6 as a percent.
items.e: 0.6 = 6 tenths = 60 hundredths = 60%. Multiply by 100. 6% would be 0.06.

items.q: Write 0.08 as a percent.
items.e: 0.08 = 8 hundredths = 8%. 80% would be 0.8.

items.q: Write 1 as a percent.
items.e: 1 is one whole, and the whole is 100%. 1% is only 0.01.

items.q: Write the shaded part of the hundred grid as a decimal.
items.e: 5 out of 100 squares = 5 hundredths = 0.05. 0.5 would be 50 squares, and 0.95 is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: Write 12 as a percent.
items.e: 12 = 50100 = 50%. 12% just writes the digits 1 and 2 together.

items.q: Write 710 as a percent.
items.e: 710 = 70100 = 70%. Multiply the top and bottom by 10. 30% is the part left over.

items.q: Write 14 as a percent.
items.e: 14 = 25100 = 25%, because 4 × 25 = 100. 14% just writes the digits together.

items.q: Write 35 as a percent.
items.e: 5 × 20 = 100, so 35 = 60100 = 60%. 35% writes the digits together, and 30% multiplies only by 10.

items.q: Write 320 as a percent.
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so 320 = 15100 = 15%. 23 is 3 + 20, and 3% forgets that the whole is 20.

items.q: Write 20% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 20% = 20100. Divide the top and bottom by 20: 15. 120 would be 5%.

items.q: Write 75% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 75% = 75100. Divide the top and bottom by 25: 34. 14 is 25%, the part left over.

items.q: Write 45% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 45% = 45100. Divide the top and bottom by 5: 920. 45 just uses the digits 4 and 5.

items.q: Write 0.25 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.25 = 25100 = 14. 25 uses the digits 2 and 5 as a fraction.

items.q: Write 4% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 4% = 4100. Divide the top and bottom by 4: 125. 14 is 25%, not 4%.

items.q: Which number is the same as 40%?
items.e: 40% = 40100 = 0.4. 0.04 is 4%, and 140 is 2.5%.

items.q: Which does not describe the shaded part of the hundred grid?
items.e: 40 of 100 squares are shaded: 40% = 0.4 = 25. 0.04 is only 4 squares.

items.q: Which is the greatest?
items.e: Change all to percents: 25 = 40%, 0.45 = 45%, 38%, 0.405 = 40.5%. The greatest is 0.45. 0.405 has more digits, but it is less than 0.45.

items.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
items.e: Change all to percents: 14 = 25%, 0.3 = 30%, 35%. Least to greatest: 14, 0.3, 35%.

items.q: What is 10% of 90?
items.e: 10% = 110. Divide by 10: 90 ÷ 10 = 9. 0.9 is 1%, and 80 subtracts 10 from 90.

items.q: What is 50% of 64?
items.e: 50% is half. 64 ÷ 2 = 32. 14 subtracts 50 from 64, and 128 doubles instead of halving.

items.q: What is 1% of 700?
items.e: 1% = 1100. Divide by 100: 700 ÷ 100 = 7. 70 is 10%, and 699 subtracts 1.

items.q: What is 25% of 36?
items.e: 25% = 14. Divide by 4: 36 ÷ 4 = 9. 18 is 50%, and 11 subtracts 25 from 36.

items.q: What is 20% of 35?
items.e: 10% of 35 = 3.5. 20% is double: 2 × 3.5 = 7. 15 subtracts 20 from 35, and 3.5 is only 10%.

items.q: What is 5% of 80?
items.e: 10% of 80 = 8. 5% is half of 10%: 4. 16 divides 80 by 5, which gives 20%.

items.q: What is 75% of 60?
What is 30% of 70?
items.e: 10% of 70 = 7. 30% = 3 × 7 = 21. 7 is only 10%, and 40 subtracts 30 from 70.

items.q: What is 15% of 60?
items.e: 15% = 10% + 5%. 10% of 60 = 6, and 5% = 3. 6 + 3 = 9. 6 and 3 are only the two steps.

items.q: What is 40% of 45?
What is 2% of 350?
What is 60% of 80?
What is 90% of 40?
items.e: 10% of 40 = 4. 90% = 100% − 10%, so 40 − 4 = 36. 4 is the 10% that is left out, and 50 adds 10 to 40.

items.q: What is 10% of 6.4?
items.e: 10% means divide by 10: 6.4 ÷ 10 = 0.64. 64 multiplies by 10, and 5.4 subtracts 1.

items.q: What is 1% of 12 000?
items.e: 1% means divide by 100: 12 000 ÷ 100 = 120. 1200 is 10%, and 12 divides by 1000.

items.q: What is 12% of 50?
items.e: 1% of 50 = 0.5. 12% = 12 × 0.5 = 6. Or: 50 is half of 100, so 12% of 50 is half of 12. 38 subtracts 12 from 50.

items.q: The whole bar is $50. What is 40% of $50?
items.e: The bar shows $50 in 10 equal parts, so each part is 10% = $5. 4 parts: 4 × $5 = $20. $5 is one part, and $10 subtracts 40 from 50.

items.q: The whole bar is 80 km. What is 75% of 80 km?
items.e: The bar shows 80 km in 4 equal parts. Each part is 25% = 80 ÷ 4 = 20 km. 3 parts: 3 × 20 = 60 km. 20 km is one part (25%), and 5 km subtracts 75 from 80.

items.q: Which is greater: 20% of 50 or 50% of 20?
items.e: 20% of 50 = 2 × 5 = 10. 50% of 20 = 20 ÷ 2 = 10. They are equal: a% of b is always b% of a.

items.q: Which has the same value as 25% of 80?
A $40 sweater is 25% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 25% = 14. $40 ÷ 4 = $10 off. Sale price: $40 − $10 = $30. $15 takes away 25 dollars instead of 25 percent, and $10 is the discount, not the price.

items.q: A $60 soccer ball is 10% off. How much money do you save?
items.e: 10% of $60 = $60 ÷ 10 = $6 saved. $54 is the sale price, and $50 takes away 10 dollars.

items.q: Hiking boots that cost $80 are 20% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $80 = $8, so 20% = $16. $80 − $16 = $64. $60 takes away 20 dollars, and $72 takes off only 10%.

items.q: A $70 rain jacket is 50% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 50% off means you pay half: $70 ÷ 2 = $35. $20 takes away 50 dollars, and $105 adds the discount.

items.q: A $120 lacrosse stick is 25% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 25% of $120 = $120 ÷ 4 = $30. $120 − $30 = $90. $95 takes away 25 dollars, and $30 is the discount.

items.q: A $45 backpack is 40% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $45 = $4.50, so 40% = $18. $45 − $18 = $27. $5 takes away 40 dollars, $18 is the discount, and $41 takes off only 4 dollars.

items.q: A $32 board game is 25% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 25% of $32 = $32 ÷ 4 = $8. $32 − $8 = $24. $7 takes away 25 dollars, $8 is the discount, and $28.80 takes off only 10%.

items.q: A $200 snowboard is 15% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $200 = $20 and 5% = $10, so 15% = $30. $200 − $30 = $170. $185 takes away 15 dollars, and $180 takes off only 10%.

items.q: An $18 puzzle is 50% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 50% is half: $18 ÷ 2 = $9. $17.50 takes away only 50¢, $16.20 takes off 10%, and $27 adds the discount.

items.q: A $65 helmet is 20% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $65 = $6.50, so 20% = $13. $65 − $13 = $52. $45 takes away 20 dollars, and $58.50 takes off only 10%.

items.q: A $12 book is 5% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $12 = $1.20, so 5% = 60¢. $12.00 − $0.60 = $11.40. $7 takes away 5 dollars, 60¢ is the discount, and $10.80 takes off 10%.

items.q: An $85 hockey jersey is 30% off. What is the sale price?
A $40 item is 25% off. Which calculation gives the sale price?
items.e: You pay what is left: 100% − 25% = 75%. So the sale price is 75% of $40 = $30. 25% of $40 = $10 is the discount.

items.q: A sign says “Pay only 70% of the price.” What percent is the discount?
items.e: You pay 70%, so you save 100% − 70% = 30%. 70% is the part you pay.

items.q: You save $9 on a $36 item. What percent is the discount?
items.e: $9 out of $36 = 936 = 14 = 25%. 9% uses the dollars as a percent, 4% is 36 ÷ 9, and 75% is the part you pay.

items.q: Skates were $50. Now they are on sale for $40. What percent is the discount?
items.e: The discount is $50 − $40 = $10. $10 out of $50 = 15 = 20%. 10% uses the $10 as a percent, and 25% compares $10 to the sale price ($40), not the old price.

items.q: The bar shows a $60 price in 5 equal parts. The shaded part is the discount. What is the sale price?
items.e: Each part is $60 ÷ 5 = $12, and 1 part is shaded, so the discount is $12 (20%). Sale price: $60 − $12 = $48. $12 is the discount, and $40 takes away 20 dollars.

items.q: Store A takes $20 off a $120 coat. Store B takes 25% off the same coat. Which store saves you more?
items.e: 25% of $120 = $120 ÷ 4 = $30. $30 > $20, so Store B saves more. ($20 out of $120 is only 16, about 17%.)

items.q: A $48 tent is 25% off. You pay with a $50 bill. How much change do you get?
items.e: 25% of $48 = $12, so the sale price is $48 − $12 = $36. Change: $50 − $36 = $14. $27 comes from taking 25 dollars off ($23), $12 is the discount, and $2 forgets the sale.

items.q: Leah paid $24 for a scarf that was 25% off. What was the price before the sale?
items.e: She paid 100% − 25% = 75% of the price. 75% = $24, so 25% = $8 and 100% = 4 × $8 = $32. Check: 25% of $32 = $8, and $32 − $8 = $24. $30 adds 25% of $24, but the 25% is of the original price.

sets.title: Word problems: sales, sports and trips around BC

items.q: Our school’s goal for the Terry Fox Run is $2000. So far we have raised $1500. What percent of the goal is that?
items.e: 15002000 = 34 = 75%. 25% is the part still to raise, and 15% is 1500 ÷ 100.

items.q: Ski rentals at Whistler cost $60 a day. During Spring Break, Hana’s family gets 15% off. What is the sale price for one day?
items.e: 10% of $60 = $6 and 5% = $3, so 15% = $9. $60 − $9 = $51. $45 takes away 15 dollars, $9 is the discount, and $54 takes off only 10%.

items.q: In November, it rained in Vancouver on 24 of the 30 days. On what percent of the days did it rain?
items.e: 2430 = 45 = 80100 = 80%. 24% forgets that the whole is 30, and 20% is the dry days.

items.q: A class of 25 students goes on a field trip to Stanley Park. 60% of them have been there before. How many students have been there before?
items.e: 10% of 25 = 2.5. 60% = 6 × 2.5 = 15 students. 10 is the other 40%, 6 is 60 ÷ 10, and 35 subtracts 25 from 60.

items.q: A soccer team won 9 of its 12 games. What percent of its games did it win?
items.e: 912 = 34 = 75%. 25% is the games it did not win, and 3% is 12 − 9.

items.q: A math test has 40 questions. Arjun gets 85% of them right. How many questions does he get right?
items.e: 10% of 40 = 4 and 5% = 2, so 85% = 8 × 4 + 2 = 34. 6 is the questions he got wrong (15%), 8.5 is 10% of 85, and 85 uses the percent as the answer.

items.q: A salmon hatchery on the Fraser River has 2000 eggs. 85% of them hatch. How many eggs hatch?
items.e: 10% of 2000 = 200 and 5% = 100, so 15% = 300 do not hatch. 2000 − 300 = 1700. 300 is the eggs that do not hatch, and 1915 subtracts 85.

items.q: A survey asks a class for its favourite sport. 35% choose hockey, 40% choose soccer and the rest choose lacrosse. What percent choose lacrosse?
items.e: All the students together are 100%. 35% + 40% = 75%, so 100% − 75% = 25%. 75% is hockey and soccer together.

items.q: An $80 hockey jersey is 25% off. Mateo pays with a $100 bill. How much change does he get?
items.e: 25% of $80 = $20, so the sale price is $60. Change: $100 − $60 = $40. $45 takes 25 dollars off ($55), $20 is the discount, and $60 is the sale price.

items.q: A fruit stand in the Okanagan sells a $20 box of cherries for 30% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $20 = $2, so 30% = $6. $20 − $6 = $14. $6 is the discount, $18 takes off only 10%, and $26 adds the discount.

items.q: There are 30 students in a class. 40% of them bike to school. How many students do not bike?
items.e: 10% of 30 = 3, so 40% = 12 students bike. 30 − 12 = 18 do not. 12 is the bikers, and 60 is the percent who do not bike (60%), not the number of students.

items.q: A Grade 6 class of 120 students goes on a field trip. 5% forget their permission form. How many students forget it?
items.e: 10% of 120 = 12. 5% is half: 6. 24 divides 120 by 5, which gives 20%, and 115 subtracts 5.

items.q: A hiking trail near Grouse Mountain is 3 km long. Lucas has hiked 60% of it. How far does he have left?
items.e: Lucas has 100% − 60% = 40% left. 10% of 3 km = 0.3 km, so 40% = 1.2 km. 1.8 km is the part already hiked, and 2.4 km is 80%.

items.q: A whale-watching boat in Victoria has 50 seats. 42 seats are full. What percent of the seats are full?
items.e: 50 × 2 = 100, so 42 × 2 = 84: 84%. 42% forgets that the whole is 50, and 16% is the empty seats.

items.q: Kai sells 54 of the 60 tickets for the school raffle. What percent of the tickets has he sold?
items.e: 5460 = 910 = 90%. 54% forgets that the whole is 60, and 10% is the tickets still to sell.

items.q: A cedar seedling is 40 cm tall. By next year it grows 25% taller. How tall is it then?
items.e: 25% of 40 cm = 40 ÷ 4 = 10 cm. It grows 10 cm: 40 + 10 = 50 cm. 65 cm adds 25 cm, 10 cm is only the growth, and 30 cm takes 25% away.

items.q: A store in Burnaby sells a $90 skateboard for 20% off. A store in Surrey sells the same skateboard for $80 with 10% off. Which sale price is lower?
items.e: Burnaby: 20% of $90 = $18, so $90 − $18 = $72. Surrey: 10% of $80 = $8, so $80 − $8 = $72. They cost the same, even though the Burnaby store gives the bigger percent off.

items.q: A pack of lacrosse balls costs $40. You can use a $5-off coupon or get 10% off. Which saves more?
items.e: 10% of $40 = $4. $5 > $4, so the $5-off coupon saves more on this price.

items.q: Owen has saved $72. A $90 bike is 25% off. After buying the bike, how much money will he have left?
items.e: 25% of $90 = $22.50, so the sale price is $90 − $22.50 = $67.50. $72 − $67.50 = $4.50. $7 comes from taking 25 dollars off ($65), $22.50 is the discount, and $18 forgets the sale.

items.q: Emma pays $42 for a jacket that is 30% off. What was the price before the sale?
items.e: She paid 100% − 30% = 70% of the price. 70% = $42, so 10% = $6 and 100% = $60. Check: 30% of $60 = $18, and $60 − $18 = $42. $54.60 adds 30% of $42, but the 30% is of the original price.
